subject: Cloud marketplace private-offer: volume & unit-price budgeting follow-up
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acmecloud.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cloud marketplace private-offer: quick follow-up on volumes & $/1M token target

Hi Tom — thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can map to an AWS private-offer SKU: 

- Your usage profile: ~30k daily active requests, average request = 1.5k tokens, peak concurrency in region = 120 qps (you mentioned bursting to 220 during end-of-month runs).
- Estimated steady-state monthly tokens: 1.3B tokens (conservative) up to 2.7B tokens (scale scenario).

To make a clean private-offer proposal we need two items from your side: 
1) Target unit economics: is there a target $/1M tokens you’re trying to hit (range is fine)?
2) Budget cadence: do you prefer a committed monthly spend, annual reserved capacity, or quarterly PO?

Attached a one-page template for the marketplace private-offer and a simple projection sheet — fill ranges in the yellow cells and I’ll draft a couple of PPU scenarios (standard vs. committed). If helpful Ben can do a short run of what 10%, 20%, 30% discount ladders look like at your projected volumes.

Next steps I propose: 
- You share preferred $/1M target or budget bands by EOD Tues (4/20).
- We return 2 private-offer sketches (monthly commit, annual commit) and an AWS marketplace SKU mapping by Fri (4/23).

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood_priv_offer_template.pdf (fillable), acme_token_projection_q2_q4.xlsx (projection template)

From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acmecloud.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.io>
Date: 2027-04-19T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud marketplace private-offer: quick follow-up on volumes & $/1M token target

Hi Jasmine — appreciate the clear asks and the templates. Quick answers from our side: 

- Budget/cadence: procurement prefers a quarterly PO for now with an option to convert to an annual commitment at the end of Q3. We can do a 3-month rolling commitment in the marketplace private-offer if the SKU supports it.
- Token economics target: Our FP&A is looking for a target in the $650–$900 per 1M tokens range given our current ARR targets. That said, if we can get a clear committed-discount ladder tied to token bands (e.g., 1B, 2B, 3B monthly thresholds) that helps.

Also attached is an internal note on peak windows — we do expect a seasonal spike in July affecting concurrency. Procurement copied to loop in contracting once you have a concrete private-offer draft.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reilly | Head of ML Platform, AcmeCloud
tom.reilly@acmecloud.io

> Attachment: acme_internal_peak_windows.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud marketplace private-offer: quick follow-up on volumes & $/1M token target

Looping in a quick internal note — Tom’s target band $650–$900/1M aligns with a mid-market enterprise profile. A few operational notes for the PO/marketplace mapping: 

- Marketplace SKU mapping: AWS private offers typically want a per-unit price and unit quantity. For LLM we model the unit as 1M tokens. For quarterly PO we can propose units = projected monthly 1M-token blocks * 3 (quarter).
- Commitment vs. burst: We should provide a committed baseline (e.g., 1.5B tokens/mo equivalent) with defined overage pricing (e.g., 1.5x the committed unit price for excess up to +50%).
- Discount ladders: propose 3 tiers for review: 0–1B = base PPU, 1B–2B = base * 0.88, >2B = base * 0.78 (these multipliers land roughly in Tom’s band depending on base).

Action items: Jasmine — can you confirm whether Acme wants the SKU defined as 1M-token units or a per-100k-token unit for the marketplace listing? Smaller unit granularity can help billing but complicates procurement language. If they want 1M unit we're good to draft.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Marketplace Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@acmecloud.io>, Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud marketplace private-offer: quick follow-up on volumes & $/1M token target

Thanks Tom — that’s really helpful. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- We’ll treat the billing unit as 1M tokens for the private-offer SKU (simpler for POs). Laura will draft two sketches: (A) quarterly PO (units = projected monthly 1M blocks *3) and (B) annual committed SKU for conversion at end of Q3.
- Ben will produce three price ladder scenarios hitting target band ($650–$900/1M) with the discount multipliers he suggested.
- We’ll include an overage rule: 150% of committed unit price for excess usage up to +50% in a quarter, after which we re-tier.

Next actions: 
1) Laura to upload the two marketplace sketches to the shared Drive and mark the recommended SKU names by EOD 4/22.
2) Ben to circulate the PPU ladders and a short P&L showing impact at 1.3B / 2.0B / 2.7B monthly token volumes by 4/23.
3) Tom/procurement to confirm quarterly PO cadence and provide billing contact for DocuSign.

I’ll draft a short summary + marketplace SKU mapping once we have the numbers and send to contracting.

Best — Jasmine
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_priv_offer_template_filled_example.pdf (internal example)
